review.summary:
Attempt 2 of the phase-19 typed-preservation chunk delivers plan item 3 and closes every finding from attempt 1 with verifiable artifacts rather than prose.

The generated projection codec now routes both halves of the decode through the crate's own JSON boundary: `tools/generate_models.py:489` decodes each vendor-added field with `crate::json_decode::from_value` and re-inserts the untouched wire value into the flattened extension map on failure, and `:495` decodes the baseline remainder with `crate::json_decode::from_value(serde_json::Value::Object(raw))`. `crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs:6002-6096` confirms the emitted result for `AttackDetailResponse`, and `generate_models.py --check` passed, so all 25 projection impls (25 occurrences of `baseline response model mismatch`) match the generator. The non-optional guard at `:472` still fails closed, `KNOWN` at `:498` still omits projection names so baseline-field extension collisions remain hard errors, and `:505` suppresses the raw entry only when the typed field is explicitly set, so an explicit replacement cannot emit duplicate keys. None of the 25 models carries a constrained `Extensions<OpenValue<..>>`, so the fallback re-insertion cannot itself fail.

The attempt-1 high finding is closed with executed evidence, not reasoning: `scripts/check-rust.py:21` redefines `json-unification` as `red-team,serde_json/arbitrary_precision`, `.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:90` already contained that feature name across both toolchains so the 47-job matrix count is preserved, and `docs/checks/phase-19-rust-1.99.0-json-unification.json` records fmt/check/clippy -D warnings/test/test --examples/doc all at exit 0 with `projection_models_preserve_large_numbers_through_the_sdk_json_boundary` passing. That test (`tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:427-444`) is well targeted: the 128-bit integer sits both in an unknown field (the flattened `Extensions` path that Serde's `Content` buffer cannot hold) and nested inside a projection value, and it decodes through `AttackOutput::parse`, the real `support::parse` boundary.

The medium finding is closed properly. `contracts/compatibility/g25/projections.json` now carries a schema-derived `conforming` witness, a `nullable` flag and a `usage` classification per row, all generated from `augment_models`' additions in `tools/g25_fixtures.py:122-127`, and `every_vendor_projection_populates_typed_values_and_preserves_nullability` (`:949-977`) asserts, for all 55 rows, that absence yields unset with no extension, the conforming witness yields a populated typed value with no extension, and null yields `Patch::Null` for nullable rows but unset-plus-extension for non-nullable rows. Because the generated `projection_state` arms are rebuilt and `--check`-guarded (`g25_fixtures.py:143-153`, `:161`), this cannot silently shrink, and it distinguishes real typed population from blanket extension fallback — including `StreamDetailResponseGoalVariant2`, whose enclosing `#[serde(untagged)]` enum (`generated.rs:170642-170649`) has an `Unknown(JsonValue)` arm that would otherwise mask a failed variant decode.

Both low findings were dispositioned rather than ignored: the request-side precedence rule is now classified (`usage: request-only` for the three `JobCreateRequestJobMetadata` variants), pinned in `tools/test_g25_generation.py:67-69`, and documented at `docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:17`; the format-count dict now renders as prose at `:47`; and the generic redacted baseline error plus the retained value copy are explicitly justified at `:19`, which is consistent with the AGENTS.md rule that formatting must not echo service values. The full 23-command phase-19 gate in `tools/check_phase.py:71-88` is recorded complete and green in the chunk checks file.

One real gap remains, and it is narrow. The 55-row and 15658-case projection coverage decodes through `serde_json::from_value` (`tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:47`), not the production `support::parse`/`json_decode::from_value` boundary, so exactly one of the 25 projection models has executed production-decoder evidence under feature unification, and the untagged-union-nested projection variant is not covered for the 128-bit case. Public field types are unchanged (the optional wrapping of vendor additions is the pre-existing phase-10 design recorded at `docs/red-team-data-plane-0.93.0-plan.md:120`, and `model-additions.json` is untouched on this branch), so there is no patch-release API risk. No blocker or high finding.

findings.description: `typed()` decodes with `serde_json::from_value`, while production decodes projection models through `crate::models::support::parse` -> `crate::json_decode::from_value` (crates/scm-sdk/src/models/support.rs:111-115). The generated projection impl's outer step is `serde_json::Map::<String,Value>::deserialize(d)` (generated.rs:6004), so its behaviour depends on which deserializer `d` is; under `serde_json/arbitrary_precision` the `OwnedValue` and plain `Value` deserializers differ precisely in numeric token handling, which is why json_decode.rs exists. As a result the 55-row `projection_roundtrip`/`projection_state` coverage (:364, :447) and the 15658-case root roundtrip (:120) prove nothing about the production decoder, and only `AttackOutput` (:427) has production-boundary evidence under feature unification. The uncovered combination that matters is a projection model reached through a `#[serde(untagged)]` enum, i.e. `StreamDetailResponseGoalVariant2` inside `StreamDetailResponseGoal` (generated.rs:170642-170649), where Serde's `Content` buffer is interposed and the 128-bit path is never exercised.
findings.required_fix: Decode through the SDK boundary in the generated test arms: emit `<T>::parse(value, Mode::Response)` (or `crate::json_decode::from_value`) instead of `serde_json::from_value` in the `projection_roundtrip` and `projection_state` arms generated at tools/g25_fixtures.py:140 and :150 for every row whose Rust type has a `SCHEMA`, and extend the large-number assertion at crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:427 to at least one union-nested projection model (`StreamDetailResponse` carrying `StreamDetailResponseGoalVariant2`) so the untagged `Content` path is covered by the recorded json-unification check.

findings.description: Advisory carry-over, now documented rather than changed. All 25 projection models collapse the baseline decode failure to `serde::de::Error::custom("baseline response model mismatch")`, discarding which field mismatched, and `:489` clones every present projection value on the success path purely to serve the error path. docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:19 states both are deliberate (redaction of service values, and a retained copy for lossless fallback), which is consistent with AGENTS.md's prohibition on formatting sensitive bodies, so this is not a required change. It does leave nested baseline mismatches harder to diagnose than for every other generated model, and the clone is unnecessary work whenever the typed decode succeeds.
findings.required_fix: Optional: include the serde error's field path without its value text in the custom message at tools/generate_models.py:495 (for example the `Error::classify`/line-column metadata only), and clone the projection value only after a failed typed decode by decoding from a borrowed `&serde_json::Value` first. If the current behaviour is kept, no change is needed beyond the existing note at docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:19.

evidence: docs/reviews/phase-19-chunk-typed-preservation-attempt-02.checks.json records 23 executed commands, all exit_code 0, matching the complete phase-19 gate list in tools/check_phase.py:71-88 item for item, with source_sha256 7edc930... and source_unchanged true. Non-trivial recorded outputs include `tools/g25_fixtures.py --check` -> {"roots": 46, "mutations": 15658, "formats": 184, "enums": 138, "typedProjectionFields": 55}, `tools/generate_models.py --check` -> {"checked": true, "outputs": 16, "graphNodes": 13018}, and `tools/g25-oracle.mts --check` -> {"roots":46,"independentOutcomes":15658}. These are executed records, not assertions.

The attempt-1 high finding is closed by executed evidence: scripts/check-rust.py:21 now defines json-unification as `--no-default-features --features red-team,serde_json/arbitrary_precision`, and docs/checks/phase-19-rust-1.99.0-json-unification.json records all six commands at exit_code 0 (check 43.4s, clippy 45.0s, test 86.2s) with the g25_response_compatibility suite running 6 tests including `projection_models_preserve_large_numbers_through_the_sdk_json_boundary` and `every_vendor_projection_populates_typed_values_and_preserves_nullability`, all ok.

.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:90 already listed `json-unification` in the feature matrix and :89 lists toolchains 1.89.0 and 1.99.0, so redefining the feature set adds the red-team projection regression to the existing matrix on both compilers without changing the 47-job count, exactly as docs/g25-response-compatibility-plan.md:138-141 claims. The separate `minimal` entry remains at :90.

Both decode halves now use the crate's JSON boundary: tools/generate_models.py:489 emits `crate::json_decode::from_value::<{typed}>(value.clone())` per projection field with `raw.insert` fallback, and :495 emits `crate::json_decode::from_value(serde_json::Value::Object(raw))` for the baseline remainder. crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs:6002-6096 shows the emitted `AttackDetailResponse` impl verbatim, and `generate_models.py --check` passing means all 25 impls (25 occurrences of `baseline response model mismatch`) are in sync with the generator.

The fallback cannot itself fail: grep for `#[serde(flatten)]extensions:Extensions<OpenValue` in crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs returns 0 matches against 25 `baseline response model mismatch` occurrences, so every projection model's extension storage is `Extensions<JsonValue>` and a re-inserted unrepresentable value always decodes into it.

The medium finding is closed by per-row state assertions, not identity: crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:949-977 iterates all 55 projections.json rows and asserts ("unset", false) for absence, ("value", false) for the schema-derived `conforming` witness, and ("null", false) for nullable rows versus ("unset", true) for non-nullable rows. tools/g25_fixtures.py:122-127 derives `conforming`, `nullable` and `usage` directly from `augment_models`' additions, :143-151 regenerates the `projection_state` arms, and :161 raises 'G25 generated fixture/binding is stale' on drift, so the coverage cannot silently shrink.

Request-side precedence is now classified, pinned and documented: contracts/compatibility/g25/projections.json carries `usage` on all 55 rows (3 request-only, 7 request-and-response, 2 standalone-schema, rest response-only), tools/test_g25_generation.py:67-69 asserts the request-only set is exactly {JobCreateRequestJobMetadataVariant1, Variant2, Variant3} and that every row has `conforming` and a boolean `nullable`, and docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:17 documents the typed-over-raw precedence for those three request models and tells callers to leave the projection unset to serialize a preserved raw value.

The report-formatting low finding is fixed: docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:47 now reads 'Format occurrences across the strict vendor response trees are `duration` 4, `rfc3339` 56, `uuid` 124; 28 operations are affected' instead of a raw Python dict, and :19 records the deliberate decisions on redacted baseline errors and the retained value copy.

No public API change in this patch: the optional wrapping of vendor-added fields at tools/red_team_dataplane.py:398-401 implements the pre-existing phase-10 design stated at docs/red-team-data-plane-0.93.0-plan.md:120 ('on existing response models remain optional to decode older deployments'), contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/model-additions.json is not among the branch's modified files so the addition set is unchanged, and tools/generate_models.py:472-473 still raises ValueError('Vendor response projections must remain optional') if any projection became required.

Serializer invariants are directly tested: crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:403-424 proves an unrepresentable value stays unset and roundtrips, an explicit typed replacement wins and emits a single key, and an extension colliding with the baseline field `uuid` still makes serialization fail. tools/generate_models.py:498 excludes projection names from `KNOWN` and :505 skips the raw entry only when the typed field is set, which matches that test.

Governance bookkeeping is honest: docs/phase-status.json:3796-3812 records the typed-preservation chunk as `revised_awaiting_round_two` with attempt 1 at total 39 and accepted false, :3842 records the attempt-1 disposition, and the other two chunks keep their own separate records. docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md continues to state that the 17 reported consumer loopback tests were not executed here.
limitations: Bash is unavailable in this session, so I could not recompute the reviewed source SHA256 (7edc930...), the checks-file hash (4c02ab1...), or `rustInputsSha256` in the Rust check reports, and I could not re-execute any command or run `git diff` against the phase-18 commit. I assessed the recorded commands, exit codes, stdout/stderr and durations as records; they are internally consistent, match the gate list in tools/check_phase.py:71-88 exactly, and have plausible wall-clock times, but I verified them as records rather than by re-running them.

Because I could not diff against the published 0.2.1 source, my conclusion that no public projection field type changed rests on the pre-existing phase-10 design statement (docs/red-team-data-plane-0.93.0-plan.md:120), the untouched contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/model-additions.json, and the generator's fail-closed optionality guard, not on a byte comparison with the published crate.

The low finding about the test decode boundary is derived by construction from the repository's own documentation of the Serde `Content` 128-bit limitation (crates/scm-sdk/src/json_decode.rs:1-12, :277-311) plus the generated code path and the untagged enum at generated.rs:170642-170649. I could not build or run anything to show a divergence, and I make no claim that the untagged-union projection path is currently broken — only that it is unverified for the 128-bit case.

generated.rs is ~183k lines. I read the full `AttackDetailResponse` projection impl (:6002-6099), the `BaselineWire` region of `AttackMultiTurnDetailResponse` (:7128-7161) and the `StreamDetailResponseGoal` enum, and relied on targeted grep counts (25 projection impls, 0 constrained extension types) plus the passing `generate_models.py --check` for the remaining impls rather than reading all 25.

The local phase-19 gate runs json-unification only on toolchain 1.99.0; MSRV 1.89.0 coverage for the red-team + arbitrary_precision combination exists only in the CI matrix (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:89-90), whose terminal receipts are a phase-20 deliverable. I did not treat this as a chunk finding, but it is not yet backed by a recorded run.

I reviewed the five declared chunk scope artifacts in depth plus the supporting files they depend on (tools/g25_fixtures.py, tools/red_team_dataplane.py, tools/test_g25_generation.py, scripts/check-rust.py, json_decode.rs, models/support.rs, docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md, the plan, PHASES.md, AGENTS.md, phase-status.json). I did not re-audit the validation-policy or regression-and-governance chunks, phase 18's accepted plan and audit, or historical release infrastructure, per the scoping instruction.
Live service acceptance and the 17 reported airs-cli-rs loopback failures remain unverified; the plan and docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md state this explicitly and I make no claim either way.
